tools.name: run_code
tools.description: Preferred way to use MCP tools when a request needs more than two tool calls: per-item fetches, pagination, joining data across servers, or counting, grouping, ranking or filtering results. Write one TypeScript/JavaScript snippet (the body of an async function) that calls your tools as async functions inside an isolated sandbox (no network, files, imports or Node APIs), and `return` only what the answer needs. Call tools as `await <server>.<tool>(input)`, for example `await github.list_pull_requests({ owner, repo, state: 'open' })`; allowed built-in tools are under `builtin` (e.g. `builtin.view`). Results are parsed JSON when possible; failed or denied calls throw. Use Promise.all for independent calls and do all counting, summing, sorting and ranking inside the code rather than in your head. One run_code call replaces many tool calls, keeps bulk data out of your context, and is cheaper, faster and more accurate. Results over ~6K tokens are truncated (the full value stays in ``); `state` persists between runs. Call search_functions first for exact signatures and return shapes. For a single small lookup, call the tool directly.

code.description: Body of an async function. Use `return` for the result.

tools.name: search_functions
tools.description: Find functions callable from run_code: returns TypeScript signatures with parameter docs and, once learned, return shapes. Use it before run_code whenever a task needs several MCP calls. Query by intent, e.g. "list pull requests" or "jira issue comments".
